entities.summary:
Clitomachus (186 BCE, Carthage) was a prominent figure in the Classical era, a time of significant cultural and philosophical developments. As a philosopher, he contributed to the ongoing debates about the nature of reality and knowledge. His ideas, though not widely recognized during his lifetime, have had a lasting impact on Western philosophy.

Clitomachus was born in Carthage, a major city in the ancient Mediterranean world. His early life and education are not well documented, but it is known that he was influenced by the philosophical ideas of the time. He spent much of his life in Carthage, where he engaged in intellectual discussions with other prominent thinkers.

The legacy of Clitomachus can be seen in the continued development of philosophical ideas in the Western tradition. His contributions to the understanding of reality and knowledge have influenced scholars for centuries, and his ideas remain relevant today.

In the annals of history, Clitomachus stands as a testament to the power of human inquiry and the enduring importance of philosophical inquiry.
